subject: Cross-cloud private offer: region constraints, pricing, and partner margin
messages:
From: Kayla Tran <kayla.tran@cityhealth.org>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, procurement@cityhealth.org
Cc: partners@medchannel.com
Date: 2026-12-18T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Private offer pricing for CityHealth (GovCloud + GCP region)

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for taking this on. CityHealth is preparing a private offer request covering two deployment footprints: AWS GovCloud (us-gov-west-1) and a GCP region constrained to us-central1 for data residency. Procurement asked that we provide:

- A private offer for each cloud with standard list-price / discount lines (we understand different marketplaces require different skus).
- A recommended reseller (channel) margin for MedChannel LLC — they'll be the partner of record and expect pass-through billing.
- Any constraints on listing price or invoice flow that would impact their revenue recognition (they typically expect a 15% margin).

Attached is our SOW draft and a short procurement timeline: PO target by 2027-01-10, final MSA signed prior. Can you confirm whether the private offer needs identical list prices across clouds for our internal billing, and share an initial discount / margin structure we can show procurement? Also flag any tax/billing caveats for GovCloud.

Thanks — Kayla

--
Kayla Tran
Senior Procurement Manager
CityHealth Network
Attachment: CityHealth_SOW_draft.pdf (application/pdf, 312 KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Kayla Tran <kayla.tran@cityhealth.org>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-19T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer pricing for CityHealth (GovCloud + GCP region)

Kayla —

Appreciate the clear timeline and the SOW. High-level answers up front:

- You do not need identical list prices across clouds; marketplaces allow discrete SKUs and list prices per cloud. For revenue routing we can map net revenue consistently back to the CityHealth contract, but pass-through mechanics differ (Azure/GCP are straightforward; AWS GovCloud has extra billing validation steps).

- For MedChannel LLC, a starting channel margin of 12–18% is reasonable depending on whether they require invoicing up-front or monthly pass-through for usage. If they need guaranteed margin on committed spend (vs. percentage of net), that typically adds complexity.

- GovCloud tax/PO note: GovCloud purchases often require specific tax-exempt documentation and a separate invoice profile; procurement should expect a slightly longer invoice turnaround (2–3 weeks) versus commercial regions.

I've attached a quick pricing workup with three scenarios (conservative, balanced, aggressive) that map list price -> discount -> partner net. Preliminary proposals:

- Conservative: 20% list discount, partner margin 18% (good for lower risk, higher list price).
- Balanced: 30% list discount, partner margin 15% (recommended for CityHealth scale and MedChannel expectations).
- Aggressive: 40% list discount, partner margin 12% (works if CityHealth commits to 12-month ARR minimum).

Questions for you:
1) Does CityHealth require the partner (MedChannel) to be on the PO or is Redwood the contracting party with partner receiving a pass-through credit?
2) Is there any internal constraint on list price floor (procurement sometimes needs a list price above $X for amortization)?

Cc'ing Jordan and Irene to weigh in on channel treatment and legal/billing. I can turn the Balanced scenario into a private offer draft once we confirm partner routing and whether GovCloud needs a separate MSA appendix.

Best,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Director, Sales — Marketplaces & Partners
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Dec 19, 2026 at 11:05 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've attached a quick pricing workup with three scenarios...

Kayla / team —

Quick operational notes from channel / ops perspective:

- For marketplace private offers we generally support two partner settlement patterns: (A) Redwood invoices CityHealth and issues a rebate to MedChannel (preferred when partner is not on the PO); (B) Partner is on the PO and Redwood issues net-amount invoices to partner (partner handles downstream billing). Option B shortens partner cash flow but requires the partner to be a validated reseller on each cloud marketplace.

- For GovCloud specifically: AWS GovCloud private offers often require the partner to be a registered GovCloud partner (specialized profile) to appear on invoices. If MedChannel is not GovCloud-enabled, we should use settlement pattern A and include a committed rebate to them.

- Margin math (balanced scenario): Example for $250k committed ARR
  * List ARR: $357k (example)
  * Redwood net (after 30% discount): $250k
  * Partner margin (15% of net): $37.5k
  * Redwood retained net: $212.5k

- Tax/invoice: when we use settlement A (rebate), the partner margin is a post-invoice credit, which can create timing differences for partners that recognize revenue on invoice date. If MedChannel needs guaranteed margin timing, we should structure net invoicing to the partner (option B) and validate their GovCloud status.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Kayla: confirm whether MedChannel must appear on the PO (procurement constraint).
2) Kayla/CityHealth: confirm committed ARR and billing cadence (monthly vs. annual upfront).
3) If they want partner on PO for GovCloud, I'll reach out to MedChannel and ops to validate GovCloud reseller enrollment — that takes ~5 business days.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if helpful.

—Jordan
Principal, Deal Ops & Marketplaces
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private offer pricing for CityHealth (GovCloud + GCP region) — approval to proceed

Team / Kayla —

Thanks for the clear options. I reviewed the balanced scenario and channel math. Approve moving forward on the Balanced proposal with a firm commercial guardrail as follows:

- Commercial: 30% off list (Balanced scenario) capped to 12 months; committed ARR = $250,000 (deal_id RLW-1782).
- Partner margin: 15% of Redwood net (rebate or pass-through per MedChannel capability).
- GovCloud special handling: if MedChannel cannot be GovCloud-enrolled within 5 business days, Ops will proceed with settlement pattern A (Redwood invoices CityHealth + rebate to MedChannel).

Action items:
- Jordan / Ops: please validate MedChannel GovCloud enrollment now. If yes, produce draft private offers for AWS GovCloud and GCP (us-central1) and share DocuSign MSA link.
- Hannah / AE: prepare procurement packet (pricing summary, SOW, payment terms) to send to CityHealth; include the revenue routing explanation (rebate vs partner-on-po).
- Kayla: confirm whether CityHealth prefers monthly invoicing or an annual invoice (this affects partner margin timing).

Linking HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345 — please update stage to "Procurement: Private Offer" and attach the SOW. I've asked legal to prep a narrow MSA appendix for GovCloud requirements; I'll route for signature after Ops finishes the offers.

Ben

Redwood Inference
